department: IMPRS for Astronomy and Cosmic Physics (IMPRS-HD)

deadline.value: Nov 3, 2026, 14:00 CET for fall 2027 entry; the application and both reference letters must arrive by then. Interviews Feb 1–5, 2027
deadline.quote: The deadline for next term (fall 2027) applications is November 3, 2026, at 14:00 CET. | Applications must have arrived by the deadline, including all material and reference letters.

also.quote: Interviews in Heidelberg will be carried out February 1-5, 2027.

gre_subject.value: Not stated on the page checked

supervisor.value: A central committee screens applications; shortlisted files go to all potential supervisors and an interested supervisor triggers an interview. The project supervisor makes the final offer
supervisor.quote: The application material of shortlisted candidates is then made available to all potential supervisors in Heidelberg. When a supervisor points out interest in an applicant, this applicant can then be considered for an invitation for an interview

also.quote: The final decision to offer a thesis project to an applicant is made by the supervisor of that project

funding.value: Official offers come with funding, typically a 3+1-year contract; MSc holders get about EUR 1,800–2,000 net/month (amount and terms depend on the funding source)
funding.quote: Together with the offer of a PhD project, financial support is offered. | if there is an “official” offer, it comes with funding. | IMPRS students holding a MSc degree equivalent will receive a fellowship for a period of three-four years with a net income of EUR 1800-2000 per month.

entry_route.value: MSc in physics or equivalent (with a substantial master's thesis) typically required; exceptional 4-year BSc holders can enter the 4+4 PhD programme
entry_route.quote: Typically, applicants must have (or expect to have) a degree equivalent to the MSc in Physics | Exceptionally qualified applicants with a 4-yr BSc degree can be accepted for PhD studies in the so-called 4+4 PhD program.

notes: Dr. rer. nat. in astrophysics; six Heidelberg institutes (MPIA, MPIK, ARI, LSW, ITA, HITS). Admitted students register with the Department of Physics and Astronomy via HGSFP. Use reference number IMPRS2027 in the application system. Germany requires a grade of 2.0 or better (about B+). Covers astronomy as well: the school offers a doctoral degree programme in astrophysics.
name: Heidelberg University and Max Planck Institute for Astronomy (MPIA)
